stem:
Meena is standing in her school playground. Her teacher asks four students to describe the position of a flag post in the ground.

Arun says: "The flag post is 12 m from the classroom wall."
Bhavna says: "The flag post is 9 m from the gate."
Chetan says: "The flag post is 15 m from the water tap."
Divya says: "The flag post is 7 m from the neem tree."

All four students measured correctly. Which statement about the reference points is correct?

options.text: Only one student can be correct, because the flag post can have only one position.
All four students are correct, because each distance is measured from a different reference point.
The reference point must always be the gate of the school.
The flag post itself is the reference point in all four measurements.

teacher.key_rationale: Each stated distance describes the flag post's position with respect to a different fixed object (wall, gate, tap, tree), and each fixed object serves as that measurement's reference point. Since all four measurements are correct, all four descriptions are valid; only the reference points differ. Option A wrongly assumes one position means one description, C invents a mandatory reference point, and D confuses the object being located with the reference point.
